subject: Materials Science
title: Zinc and Galvanizing
description: A 60-second lesson on Zinc and Galvanizing.

hook.text: Highway guardrails sit in rain for decades and never rust through. Thank zinc.

buildup.text: Galvanizing dips steel into molten zinc, coating it with a sacrificial armor layer.

discovery.text: Zinc corrodes first, sacrificing itself to protect the steel underneath.

twist.text: Even if the coating is scratched, zinc still protects nearby exposed steel electrically.

climax.text: Half of all zinc produced globally goes to galvanizing — protecting infrastructure worldwide.

punchline.text: Zinc dies so steel can live.

quiz.question: How does galvanizing protect steel?
options: Zinc melts and fills cracks in the steel
Zinc corrodes first, sacrificing itself for the steel
Zinc makes steel harder and stronger
